facts.fact: The health ministry's Plan National de Développement Sanitaire 2021-2025 states that DHIS 2, its tool for managing routine data, is deployed in all regional and departmental health directorates, all regional hospital centres (CHR) and general hospitals (HG) and in a few first-contact health establishments (ESPC); it gives no count of those ESPC and no date, so the date is the plan's published date.

The Plan National de Développement Sanitaire 2021-2025 says the ministry keeps both paper and electronic tools for regular reporting, that DHIS 2 is deployed in every departmental health directorate and only a few first-contact establishments, and that district reports reached 100% completeness and 98.23% timeliness in 2020; the deployment statement is undated, so the date is the plan's published date.

The Plan National de Développement Sanitaire 2021-2025 presents DHIS 2 as one of the electronic reporting tools developed by the ministry in charge of health, and cites the ministry's directorate DIIS with DHIS2 as the source of its routine figures; the statement is undated, so the date is the plan's published date.

The health ministry's costed Plan National de Développement Sanitaire 2021-2025, dated October 2021, names DHIS 2 in its activities: making DHIS 2 interoperable with SIRHS, MAGPI, DVD-MT and M-TBVIH at 30 million FCFA a year for 2021 to 2025, and bringing the private sector, national public establishments and other bodies not yet enrolled into the SIG (DHIS 2) at 30 million FCFA a year; the passages read do not say who pays.

The Plan National de Développement Sanitaire 2021-2025 lists the DPI (Dossier Patient Informatisé), meant to automate the patient's pathway within a hospital, as under experimentation; it names no site, no count and no primary clinic using it, and gives no date, so the date is the plan's published date.

The Plan National de Développement Sanitaire 2021-2025 lists the DPI (Dossier Patient Informatisé) among the electronic tools developed by the ministry in charge of health; the statement is undated, so the date is the plan's published date.

The health ministry's costed Plan National de Développement Sanitaire 2021-2025, dated October 2021, carries an activity to make available or dematerialise the harmonised collection tools, including the patient record, at all levels of the health pyramid, at 31 million FCFA a year for 2021 to 2025, and counts electronic medical records (DME) among the digital health tools it refers to; the activity does not name the DPI and the passages read do not say who pays.
